text:
David Perron scored his first goal as a Dallas Star on Nov 12 against Winnipeg, the 333rd of his career, in his 20th NHL season. Yardbarker noted the timing. He's 38, on his eighth NHL team, and a Stanley Cup winner with St. Louis in 2019.

The role is small: 10:46 a night, down almost three minutes from his recent games, on a Dallas team that keeps winning around him. That night against the Jets was his best of the year, six shots in 14:30. He has one point in nine games.

The numbers don't flatter him. At five on five the Stars get 42% of the expected goals with him on, about nine points worse than when he sits. NHL Edge has his speed near the bottom of the league. Evolving-Hockey had a different picture last season, with Perron taking chances away at the 94th percentile.

What to watch: whether he can find a lane on the power play or settles into a part-time depth job. At this stage of a long career, either would be honest work.
